metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (COBOL) with a deployable entry point (PAYRUN batch program executed via JCL) and a dependency on DB2 database.
metadata.archetype_justification: The system has persistent state (IBM DB2 for z/OS, VSAM indexed files) and performs write operations (generates payroll output files). No message queue consumers detected, no multi-service orchestration.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.05 yields Not Ready band (< 1.5) but 11 High findings yields Remediation Required tier (2-11 High rule). This is a legacy mainframe system with near-zero cloud readiness across all surfaces. The score-based band more accurately reflects system state.

findings.title: All compute on mainframe with no managed AWS services
findings.description: All compute runs on an IBM z/OS mainframe (COBOL batch) with a single EC2 m4.large instance used as a plaintext FTP file gateway. No managed container orchestration or serverless services are used.
findings.gap: No managed AWS compute services for the primary workload. Mainframe is on-premises with no path to managed compute without application rewrite.
findings.recommendation: Migrate payroll processing to AWS managed compute — AWS Batch or ECS Fargate for batch workloads, or Lambda for event-driven processing.

findings.title: Database fully self-managed on mainframe
findings.description: IBM DB2 for z/OS v10 running self-managed on the mainframe. VSAM indexed files serve as primary data access. No AWS managed database services used.
findings.gap: All data persistence is self-managed on proprietary mainframe infrastructure with no automated failover, scaling, or managed patching.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL. Use AWS DMS and SCT for schema conversion and data migration from DB2.

findings.title: Workflow orchestration hardcoded in JCL
findings.description: Workflow orchestration handled by JCL and CA-7 job scheduler. Two-step sequential workflow with no managed workflow service, no error handling beyond JCL condition codes.
findings.gap: No managed workflow orchestration (Step Functions, MWAA). Multi-step workflow entirely hardcoded in JCL.
findings.recommendation: Implement AWS Step Functions to orchestrate the payroll workflow with error handling and retry logic.

findings.title: No messaging infrastructure — FTP only
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. System uses plaintext FTP for file transfer between mainframe and EC2 gateway with no queuing, event notification, or delivery guarantees.
findings.gap: No managed messaging (SQS, SNS, EventBridge) or streaming for data transfer. FTP provides no delivery confirmation or retry capability.
findings.recommendation: Replace FTP with Amazon S3 + EventBridge for file delivery with event notifications, or SQS for message-based integration.

findings.title: No network security controls — plaintext FTP with PII
findings.description: No VPC, security groups, or network segmentation defined. Sensitive payroll data (SSN, bank accounts) transmitted in cleartext over FTP to EC2 at hardcoded IP 10.0.7.40.
findings.gap: No network security controls. PII transmitted in cleartext with no encryption in transit, no VPC isolation, no security groups.
findings.recommendation: Implement VPC with private subnets. Replace FTP with AWS Transfer Family (SFTP) or direct S3 upload with VPC endpoints. Enforce TLS for all data movement.

findings.title: No API entry point — direct FTP to EC2
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or managed entry point. Only external interface is direct FTP to EC2 at hardcoded IP with no throttling, authentication beyond FTP credentials, or traffic management.
findings.gap: No managed entry point. Direct FTP to EC2 with no security controls, no throttling, no request validation.
findings.recommendation: Implement API Gateway with throttling and authentication for modernized endpoints. Use AWS Transfer Family for file-based integration.

findings.title: No auto-scaling — static mainframe capacity
findings.description: No auto-scaling mechanisms. Mainframe has static capacity. EC2 m4.large is a single instance with no ASG. Batch window overruns indicate insufficient static capacity.
findings.gap: All capacity statically provisioned with no ability to scale. Batch overruns are a symptom of fixed capacity.
findings.recommendation: When migrated, implement auto-scaling via AWS Batch (managed scaling) or ECS/EKS auto-scaling for the compute layer.

findings.title: No backup or recovery configuration
findings.description: No automated backup configuration defined. DB2 and VSAM files on mainframe with no visible backup retention, PITR, or restore procedures. JCL GDG provides limited output versioning only.
findings.gap: No automated backup or recovery procedures defined in code. No restore testing documented.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated backups when migrating: PITR on Aurora/RDS, S3 versioning, AWS Backup plan covering all data stores.

findings.title: Zero Infrastructure as Code
findings.description: No IaC files exist. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or any other IaC. All infrastructure manually provisioned and maintained.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. All infrastructure manually created with no reproducibility, no version control of infrastructure state.
findings.recommendation: Begin IaC adoption immediately. Define EC2 gateway and networking in Terraform or CloudFormation. Ensure all new AWS resources are defined in IaC from day one.

findings.title: No CI/CD automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, CodeBuild, or pipeline definition. Source header warns 'DO NOT RECOMPILE WITHOUT CONTACTING MAINFRAME TEAM'. Source only added to version control in 2021.
findings.gap: All deployments manual. No automated build, test, or deploy stages. Changes require manual coordination.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline + CodeBuild or GitHub Actions) with build, test, and deploy stages with automated rollback.

findings.title: COBOL — no AWS SDK or cloud-native tooling
findings.description: Application written in COBOL (Enterprise COBOL 4.2) with JCL orchestration. COBOL has no AWS SDK, no cloud-native tooling, and extremely limited developer talent pool.
findings.gap: COBOL has no AWS SDK support and no cloud-native development path. Original author retired in 2014.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite payroll logic in a modern language with full AWS SDK support (Java 21/Spring Boot 3.x, Python 3.12, TypeScript/Node.js 20, or Go 1.22).

findings.title: Tightly-coupled monolith — single COBOL program
findings.description: Single COBOL program with no module boundaries, no separation of concerns. All business logic in one procedural program with pervasive shared state via WORKING-STORAGE.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith. Cannot independently scale, deploy, or modify individual business capabilities.
findings.recommendation: Decompose into independent services: Employee Data, Payroll Calculation, Tax Computation, Payment Disbursement, Reporting. See Decomposition Strategy.

findings.title: All communication synchronous — no async patterns
findings.description: All communication synchronous. COBOL reads files sequentially, processes records, writes output synchronously, then FTP pushes result. If FTP fails, entire batch fails with no retry.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous with no async patterns. FTP failure blocks the entire payroll output pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Implement asynchronous integration: SQS or EventBridge for payroll output delivery, S3 with event notifications instead of synchronous FTP.

findings.title: 5-7 hour batch runs with no checkpointing
findings.description: Payroll batch runs 5-7 hours synchronously with no status polling, callbacks, or checkpointing. If the job fails at hour 6, all work is lost. Sometimes overruns its window.
findings.gap: 5-7 hour batch entirely synchronous. No checkpointing, no progress reporting, no ability to resume from failure.
findings.recommendation: Implement async batch processing with checkpointing via Step Functions or AWS Batch. Add per-record/per-chunk processing with DynamoDB progress tracking.

findings.title: No API versioning — fixed-width files with no schema
findings.description: No API versioning. System uses fixed-width flat files with no schema definition, no versioning, no backward compatibility. README notes 'Fixed-width file formats with no schema/versioning'.
findings.gap: No versioning on data contract. Format changes break all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Adopt API versioning from day one when modernizing. For file interfaces during transition, use JSON Schema or Avro with schema registry.

findings.title: All endpoints hardcoded — no service discovery
findings.description: All service endpoints hardcoded. JCL contains hardcoded IP (10.0.7.40) for EC2 gateway. Dataset names hardcoded. No dynamic resolution.
findings.gap: No service discovery. All endpoints and resource locations are hardcoded with no dynamic resolution.
findings.recommendation: Use environment variables or AWS Cloud Map for service endpoints. Externalize all configuration.

findings.title: Data locked in mainframe file systems
findings.description: All data stored on mainframe file systems — VSAM indexed files and GDG for output. Output delivered as fixed-width flat files via FTP to EC2 local filesystem. No S3 or managed object storage.
findings.gap: Data locked in mainframe and EC2 local storage with no managed object storage, no accessibility for analytics.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to S3 as primary storage. Implement data parsing pipeline (Glue or Lambda) to convert fixed-width files to structured formats.

findings.title: No data access layer — inline file I/O
findings.description: No unified data access layer. COBOL program directly accesses VSAM indexed files via inline FILE-CONTROL and FD declarations with no abstraction.
findings.gap: No data access abstraction. File I/O directly embedded in business logic with no separation of concerns.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository/DAO pattern with clear interfaces when rewriting. Enable independent evolution of data layer.

findings.title: IBM DB2 v10 — 5+ years past end-of-support
findings.description: IBM DB2 for z/OS v10 reached end-of-support April 2020. Running unsupported database engine with no security patches, no version pinning in IaC, no upgrade procedure.
findings.gap: Database engine 5+ years past EOL. No vendor support, no security patches, compliance risk.
findings.recommendation: Migrate directly to Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL. Do not upgrade DB2 in-place. Use AWS SCT and DMS.

findings.title: Proprietary data access patterns (VSAM, DB2)
findings.description: Business logic in COBOL application layer (not stored procedures), but system relies on proprietary VSAM indexed file access (z/OS-specific) and IBM DB2 (commercial). Data access patterns tightly coupled to IBM mainframe technology.
findings.gap: Tightly coupled to proprietary IBM data access patterns (VSAM, DB2) that cannot be directly migrated to open-source alternatives.
findings.recommendation: Extract payroll logic into modern language with standard database drivers. Use AWS SCT to assess DB2 schema conversion complexity.

findings.title: No encryption at rest — PII stored in plaintext
findings.description: No encryption at rest. VSAM files contain SSN (EMP-SSN PIC 9(09)) and bank accounts (EMP-ACCT PIC X(17)) in plaintext. EC2 receives unencrypted files via FTP.
findings.gap: Zero encryption at rest. Sensitive PII stored in plaintext on mainframe and EC2 filesystem.
findings.recommendation: Implement encryption at rest on all data stores. Use KMS customer-managed keys for Aurora/RDS, SSE-KMS for S3, encrypted EBS volumes.

findings.title: No API authentication — static FTP credentials only
findings.description: No proper authentication. Only external interface uses static FTP credentials (username/password) hardcoded in JCL. No OAuth2, JWT, or token-based auth.
findings.gap: No proper authentication mechanism. Static FTP credentials with no rotation, no audit trail, no revocation capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT via API Gateway with Cognito authorizers. Use AWS Transfer Family with IAM authentication for file integration.

findings.title: No centralized identity — standalone credentials
findings.description: No centralized identity provider. System uses standalone FTP credentials with no OIDC, SAML, SSO, or external IdP federation.
findings.gap: No centralized identity management. Authentication isolated with no consistent access policies.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with centralized IdP (Cognito or enterprise IdP via OIDC/SAML). Implement SSO for modernized services.

findings.title: Plaintext credentials in version control
findings.description: Plaintext FTP credentials committed to version control: username 'payroll' and password 'PayR0ll2003!' in PAYRUN.jcl. JCL comment confirms DB2 credentials also hardcoded.
findings.gap: Critical: plaintext credentials in source control accessible to anyone with repo access. Password appears from 2003 with no rotation.
findings.recommendation: Immediate: rotate exposed credentials, move all secrets to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation, remove plaintext from JCL, scan git history.

findings.title: No compute hardening or patching strategy
findings.description: No patching strategy or vulnerability scanning. EC2 gateway has no SSM Patch Manager, no Inspector, no hardened AMI. m4.large is previous-generation. DB2 v10 has no available patches.
findings.gap: No patching strategy for any compute. EC2 likely unpatched. No vulnerability scanning.
findings.recommendation: Implement SSM Patch Manager for EC2 immediately. Enable Inspector. Use hardened images (Bottlerocket, AL2023) when modernizing.

findings.title: No application security pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning configured. No SAST, no dependency scanning, no container scanning, no security validation. No pipeline exists to integrate scanning into.
findings.gap: Zero security automation. No scanning of any kind.
findings.recommendation: Include SAST (CodeGuru/Semgrep) and dependency scanning from day one when establishing CI/CD. Implement security gate blocking on critical findings.

findings.title: No distributed tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing instrumented. No X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry, no trace ID propagation. COBOL has no instrumentation capability.
findings.gap: No tracing. Cannot trace request flow from mainframe through FTP to EC2 gateway.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with X-Ray or OpenTelemetry from day one when modernizing. Implement trace ID propagation across all service boundaries.

findings.title: No SLO definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no monitoring. README notes batch 'sometimes overruns' — implicit SLO violation with no tracking.
findings.gap: No SLO definitions, no monitoring, no error budget. Batch overruns noticed reactively.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs: batch completion within window, zero calculation errors, 100% employee coverage. Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: No business metrics
findings.description: No custom business metrics published. No visibility into employees processed, payroll amounts, error rates by category.
findings.gap: No business metrics. No visibility into whether payroll run produces correct results.
findings.recommendation: Publish business metrics: employees_processed, total_payroll_amount, processing_errors. Use CloudWatch custom metrics with dashboards.

findings.title: No alerting or anomaly detection
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection. Problems discovered manually after the fact.
findings.gap: No alerting or anomaly detection. Failures not detected until manual observation.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms on batch duration, error rates, record count anomalies. Use Anomaly Detection for payroll amount variations.

findings.title: No automated tests
findings.description: No automated tests exist. No integration tests, no unit tests, no test files. README: 'No automated tests; changes validated in a shared QA region only.'
findings.gap: Zero test coverage. Any code change carries regression risk with no safety net.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated testing as prerequisite for code changes. Start with integration tests validating payroll calculations against known inputs/outputs.

findings.title: No observability ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS, no dashboards, no named alarm owners. No monitoring infrastructure exists to own.
findings.gap: No observability assets. No dashboards, alarms, SLOs, or team attribution.
findings.recommendation: Establish observability ownership from day one: CODEOWNERS for monitoring configs, per-service dashboards, SLO definitions with team attribution.
